## workflow pr

Open a pull or merge request for the current branch

### Synopsis

Compose a pull request for the checked-out branch from its commits, the
issue and the repository's template — the same as the interface — pushing the
branch first when it is not yet on its remote. A preview — the title, the
branches, and the whole body — is confirmed first.

The code owners of the paths the branch changes, as CODEOWNERS on the base names
them, are asked to review it; the preview lists them.

--title and --body stand in for the title and description composed, and
--template names the repository's template the description starts from;
--reviewer asks the people and teams it names in place of the code owners;
--draft opens it as a draft; and --base merges it into another branch, drafting
the title and description from the commits past it and asking its code owners.

Once it is open, it offers — as the interface does — to link it on the branch's
issue, then to move the issue to the review status (jira.review_status). With
messaging set up, it ends by naming the next step, workflow announce, on stderr;
with --announce, it previews the announcement on stderr instead and waits in the
foreground for the pull request's CI to pass, then announces it, as
workflow announce --when-green does. A draft is not announced, so --announce
refuses --draft.

--json prints what was opened, and each offer and whether it was taken, as one
JSON object on stdout — under --dry-run, the pull request it would open — and
says everything else, the preview included, on stderr.

```
workflow pr [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  workflow --dry-run pr                     # what pr would push and open
  workflow pr --yes                         # push, open, link and move, without asking
  workflow pr --yes --json | jq .pull.url   # the same, and the address it opened
  workflow pr --draft --base release        # a draft into release, asking its code owners
  workflow pr --yes --announce              # open it, then announce it once CI passes
```

### Options

```
      --announce        once it is open, wait for its CI to pass, then announce it
      --base BRANCH     merge into BRANCH instead of the base the branch left; its code owners are asked to review
      --body TEXT       the whole description, TEXT, in place of the one composed from the template and the commits
      --draft           open it as a draft
  -h, --help            help for pr
  -j, --json            print what was opened, and the offers that followed, as JSON
      --reviewer NAME   ask NAME to review instead of the code owners, org/team asking a team; repeat it, or separate names with commas
      --template NAME   start the description from the repository's template NAME instead of its first
      --title TEXT      the title, TEXT, in place of the one composed
  -y, --yes             go ahead without asking: push the branch when it needs it, open the pull request, link it on the issue and move the issue to the review status
```
